analysis: The tape's story flipped twice in two hours and both flips stuck: August PCE printed soft, then final Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% — hot growth plus cooling inflation is the soft-landing combination, and October hike odds collapsed from ~68% Tuesday morning to ~35% (per WSJ live coverage). One caution: the GDP strength is history (Q2) and the PCE softness is partly the BEA methodology revision, so Friday's jobs report is now the week's live event — a strong print could re-price the hike just as fast. Under the surface, the AI trade is bifurcating: Nvidia got policy cover at the White House AI lunch and semiconductors are bidding into Micron's print tonight, while Meta's Muse-driven rally met its first serious skepticism (StoneX ROIC note plus OpenAI's Dots launch) and Meta led Nasdaq-100 laggards early. What changed vs the 6am brief: GDP released and surprised to the upside (it was a watch item), ADP beat expectations, Meta turned from flat to an early laggard on fresh analyst pushback, and early-session leadership rotated toward Nebius/Intel/Micron. Noise to discount: quarter/month-end flows can exaggerate moves into the close — stick with the confirmed data reads (PCE, GDP, ADP) over intraday quote chatter.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Final Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% annualized (from 1.5%), beating expectations of no revision: consumer spending +3.8%, business investment +9% on the AI buildout, and real final sales to private domestic purchasers at 4.6% — strongest since Q1 2023. The Dow opened higher on the read and October hike odds were pared to ~35%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hot growth alongside cooler inflation is the soft-landing mix the tape wants — it validates the PCE relief bid, though strong growth keeps the 'higher for longer' risk alive if Friday's jobs report runs hot.

headlines.headline: ADP: private employers added 90K jobs in September vs 70K expected, rebounding from a revised 36K in August. Education/health +55K, leisure/hospitality +22K, financial activities -16K; base pay +3.2% y/y.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hiring rebounded after a three-month slowdown — sets up Friday's NFP (expected +90K, unemployment 4.1%) as the week's main event for the Fed-hike debate.

headlines.headline: Meta is -1%+ in early trading, a Nasdaq-100 laggard: StoneX's Zgutowicz warned Muse's materially higher infrastructure intensity adds to — not relieves — the ROIC/capex debate; OpenAI launched paid 'Dots' AI agents on Tuesday, and Meta expanded Muse to small businesses the same day. The stock is up ~25% over the past month.
headlines.why_it_matters: The first serious skepticism note after the Muse-driven September rally — it tests whether the AI-agent narrative holds into October earnings.

headlines.headline: Nvidia is +1.5% in early trading after Trump's White House AI lunch backed industry self-regulation: CEOs signed a voluntary AI-safety accord and there was no mention of curbing data-center buildout or chip supply. The stock is on track for a third straight monthly gain.
headlines.why_it_matters: Policy overhang removed for the AI hardware trade — a constructive setup into Micron's after-close earnings, tonight's AI-hardware verdict.

headlines.headline: Just after the open: S&P 500 +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.5%, Dow a fraction lower; SPY +0.4%, QQQ +0.5%. The 10-year ticked lower to 5.24%, WTI ~$91.20, bitcoin ~$84,200. Early leaders: Nebius +~4%, Intel +~3%, Micron +~1% ahead of its earnings; laggards: AppLovin -3%, Meta -1%+.
headlines.why_it_matters: Breadth is narrow but green — semiconductors bidding ahead of tonight's Micron print while the Dow lags, a rotation-flavored open on the data.
